title: DiVeQ: Differentiable Vector Quantization Using the Reparameterization Trick
claim: A non-differentiable hard quantization step blocks gradients; replacing it with a reparameterized error-vector version lets gradients flow end to end.
layout: 3 panels, left-to-right, dashed zoom-in expanding module into formulas
description: Left, a VQ autoencoder chain: input x goes to an encoder E, then z, then a VQ box, then ẑ, then decoder D, then output x_r. Beside the VQ box, the gradient ∂ẑ/∂z is struck through in red to show the blocked gradient. The middle panel repeats the same chain with a DiVeQ box in place of VQ. Its gradient ∂z_q/∂z is shown in blue and the rest of the gradient chain is intact. Dashed lines zoom from the DiVeQ box into a dashed rounded panel on the right. That panel shows a codebook row c_1…c_K with the selected codeword c_i* highlighted in light blue. An arrow from the codeword feeds a summation node on the z → z_q path. The panel also gives the formulas z_q = z + ||c_i* − z||·sg[v_d/||v_d||] and v_d = v + c_i* − z with v ~ N(0, σ²I). The eye goes first to the red and blue gradient contrast.
caption: We replace the non-differentiable VQ operation ({\color{red} $\hat{\vz} = \vc_{i^*} = \arg\min_{\vc_j} \|\vz-\vc_j\|_2$}) on the left with differentiable vector quantization (DiVeQ) on the right that lets the gradients flow.
abstract: Vector quantization is common in deep models, yet its hard assignments block gradients and hinder end-to-end training. We propose DiVeQ, which treats quantization as adding an error vector that mimics the quantization distortion, keeping the forward pass hard while letting gradients flow. We also present a space-filling variant (SF-DiVeQ) that assigns input to a curve constructed by the lines connecting codewords, resulting in less quantization error and full codebook usage. Both methods train end-to-end without requiring auxiliary losses or temperature schedules. In VQ-VAE image compression, VQGAN image generation, and DAC speech coding tasks across various data sets, our proposed methods improve reconstruction and sample quality over alternative quantization approaches.
